subject.title: /stop abort leaves streaming card in idle state, blocking subsequent messages (replies=0)

question: Should the next repair target shared active-abort admission, Feishu streaming-card settlement, or both after a live Feishu `/stop` trace?
rationale: The source evidence crosses shared reply-run ownership and Feishu CardKit cleanup, and choosing only one side could preserve the other half of the zero-reply failure.

options.title: Trace then fix both boundaries
options.body: Capture a live current-main Feishu `/stop` trace and repair the shared admission and Feishu card settlement paths that the trace proves stale.

options.title: Patch shared admission first
options.body: Treat the busy active-abort zero-reply path as the canonical bug and add Feishu proof after the shared regression test changes.

options.title: Patch Feishu card cleanup first
options.body: Focus on closing or discarding the stale streaming card after `/stop`, accepting that shared admission may need a follow-up if zero-reply dispatch still reproduces.

recommendation.title: Trace then fix both boundaries
recommendation.body: Capture a live current-main Feishu `/stop` trace and repair the shared admission and Feishu card settlement paths that the trace proves stale.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent dispatch/session admission history and prior review context make this the best routing candidate for deciding the shared-versus-Feishu repair boundary.
